source_publication.citation: Boverio, A.; van Beek, H. L.; Savino, S.; Ranoux, A.; Huijgen, W. J. J.; Raaijmakers, H. W. C.; Fraaije, M. W.; Loncar, N. Biochemical and Structural Characterization of a Uronic Acid Oxidase from Citrus sinensis. ChemCatChem 2023, 15, e202300847.

extraction_metadata.schema: StrendaBiocatalysis (retrieved live from the STRENDA-Biocat MCP connector)
extraction_metadata.identity_note: The paper characterizes four candidate uronic acid oxidases from C. sinensis (URAOCs1-Cs4), but performs full kinetic, thermostability, structural and applied characterization only on URAOCs3 (XP_006468446.1). URAOCs1 (accession KDO75192.1, 570 aa, calculated 63678 Da) is a different protein, independently identified by proteomics from native orange-peel extract (Figure S2), used only in the initial screening comparison. This extraction treats URAOCs3 as 'the biocatalyst' and never merges data from the two.
extraction_metadata.flag_convention: Fields with "stated_in_paper": false contain information not explicitly written in the source text; each carries its own "basis" citation and is not presented as a finding of the paper.

identity.name: URAOCs3 (uronic acid oxidase, Citrus sinensis)

ec_number_note.value: Likely EC 1.1.3.- (oxidoreductase acting on CH-OH with O2 as acceptor), by analogy to other VAO-family carbohydrate oxidases
ec_number_note.basis: General EC nomenclature (IUBMB/ExplorEnz, https://www.enzyme-database.org); not assigned by the authors

identity.molecular_weight_basis: apparent mass on SDS-PAGE, single band, enzyme is glycosylated (p.3; Figure S3)
identity.catalyzed_reaction: Oxidation of uronic acids (D-galacturonic acid, D-glucuronic acid) with concomitant H2O2 formation; selective oxidation of D-galacturonic acid to galactaric acid demonstrated in pure solution and in complex carbohydrate mixtures

sequences.note: Full sequence not printed in paper or SI for URAOCs3; available only via external accession XP_006468446.1 (NCBI). Not reproduced here because it is not text present in the source document.

production_organism: Escherichia coli (strain ORIGAMI2; cloning host NEB10β)
identity.posttranslational_modification: Bicovalent FAD attachment (8α-N1-histidyl to His89; 6-S-cysteinyl to Cys151); N-linked glycosylation (single N-linked GlcNAc modeled at Asn49); intramolecular disulfide bridge Cys12-Cys74
identity.notes: Accession identifiers given in paper: URAOCs1 = KDO75192.1, URAOCs2 = KDO48902.1, URAOCs3 = XP_006468446.1, URAOCs4 = KDO77595.1; the four share >82% pairwise sequence identity (p.3).

e_coli_route.purpose: kinetics, substrate scope, thermostability, activity assays

self_produced_details.plasmid_specifications: pBAD-His-SUMO vector, N-terminal His-SUMO fusion, arabinose-inducible (araBAD promoter); synthetic gene E. coli codon-optimized with BsaI sites, Golden Gate cloning
self_produced_details.host_strains: Cloning: E. coli NEB10β RbCl (heat-shock 42°C/30s); Expression: E. coli ORIGAMI2
self_produced_details.culture_conditions: Pre-inoculum 5 mL LB + 50 µg/mL ampicillin overnight 30°C; then 2 L baffled flask, 400 mL Terrific Broth + 50 µg/mL ampicillin + 0.02% L-arabinose, 17°C for 72 h
self_produced_details.harvesting_method: Centrifugation 4950 x g, 20 min, 4°C; pellets flash-frozen at -20°C
self_produced_details.cell_disruption_process: Resuspension in buffer A (50 mM KPi, 150 mM NaCl, pH 7.7) with 0.10 mM PMSF, 0.5 mg/mL lysozyme, 1 mg/mL DNase; sonication 5 s on/5 s off, 70% amplitude, 15 min total; clarified 19800 x g, 1 h, 4°C
self_produced_details.purification_method: IMAC on TALON (Co2+) resin via His-SUMO tag; wash with buffer A then buffer B (+5 mM imidazole); elution with buffer C (+150 mM imidazole); all buffers 50 mM KPi/150 mM NaCl pH 7.7; single-step
self_produced_details.purity_specification: Single band on SDS-PAGE (~70 kDa); no numeric % purity reported
self_produced_details.storage_buffer: 50 mM KPi, 150 mM NaCl, 10% glycerol, pH 7.7
self_produced_details.yield: ~20 mg purified URAOCs3 per 1 L culture broth after single IMAC step

self_produced_details.plasmid_specifications: pPICZα vector with export/secretion tag; synthetic DNA (Twist Bioscience), P. pastoris codon-optimized, Gibson-cloned; primers in Table S1
self_produced_details.host_strain: P. pastoris X-33, transformed by electroporation (Bio-Rad MicroPulser) of SacI-linearized vector
self_produced_details.selection: YPDS-agar with increasing zeocin (100, 200, 500 µg/mL); 16 colonies screened; 2 transformants showed ~30 mU/mL galacturonic acid oxidase activity in culture filtrate
self_produced_details.induction: Rich medium (YPD) 48 h at 28°C; then 1% methanol induction (2% methanol solution in YP, doubling culture volume), further 1% methanol at 56, 72, 80 h; harvested at 96 h (4950 x g, 20 min, 4°C)
self_produced_details.purification_method: Size-exclusion chromatography, Superdex200 10/300 (Cytiva), ÄKTA pure, monitored at A280/A450; peak fractions pooled and concentrated to 18 mg/mL

biocatalyst.activity_determination_method: Hydrogen peroxide release measured via HRP-coupled chromogenic assay (AAP/DCHBS substrates), absorbance at 515 nm (epsilon515 = 26 mM^-1 cm^-1), Biotek Synergy H1 microplate reader
biocatalyst.concentration_determination_method: Extinction coefficient of covalently (6-S-cysteinyl) bound flavin, epsilon445 = 11.6 mM^-1 cm^-1 (as reported by the authors)

immobilization.notes: Only free (non-immobilized), purified soluble enzyme used in all reported experiments; no immobilization data given.

storage.additives: 50 mM KPi, 150 mM NaCl, 10% glycerol, pH 7.7
storage.notes: Storage temperature/duration and activity-retention-over-storage are not reported. Thermal-stability (Tm) data describe assay-condition conformational stability, not storage stability.

results.note: attributed by authors to trace short oligomers/monomers

substrates_screened_table1.note: A separate, earlier 16-sugar screen (10 mM substrate) on the native peel-isolated enzyme is described qualitatively only (p.2) and not tabulated with numeric values.

substrates_kinetic_and_applied.amount: 1 g syrup (19.4% w/w GalA, 52.6 Bx) diluted in 54.4 mL water -> target 0.35 wt% GalA
11.4 wt% GalA (total dry matter), diluted to 0.36 wt%
substrates_kinetic_and_applied.note: Result described qualitatively only; no numeric table/figure given

substrates_kinetic_and_applied.basis: FAD-dependent oxidases of the VAO family require O2 as terminal electron acceptor, generating H2O2 (standard flavo-oxidase mechanism; refs [15]-[17] cited in the paper; general background: Fraaije & van Berkel, J. Biotechnol. 2000). Not explicitly named or quantified in this paper.

products.evidence: Quantified by HPLC (Ionpak KC-811, PDA 210 nm) as product of D-galacturonic acid oxidation, in pure solution (Fig. 4B) and pectin hydrolysate (Fig. 4A); up to 0.364 wt% measured after 24 h from pectin hydrolysate feed
Basis of all activity assays (HRP-coupled chromogenic detection); removed in conversion experiments by co-added catalase

products.note: Expected by analogy from D-glucuronic acid oxidation but not chemically confirmed or named as a product anywhere in the paper; only galactaric acid is verified.

other_components.effect: inhibitory; 500 mM -> 50% residual activity; no effect on Tm

other_components.amount: 135 kU/mL stock, 1.0 µL per 25-26 mL reaction

other_components.note: Not a catalytic reaction component; listed for completeness

operation_mode.notes: All reported reactions (assays, kinetics, both selective-conversion experiments) are single-batch; no continuous or fed-batch operation described.

system.notes: Single aqueous phase in every experiment; no multiphasic/biphasic or gas-fed system described.

reaction_conditions.pH_detection_note: Not specified in the paper (no electrode model, calibration, or measurement temperature given).

vessel.notes: read on Biotek Synergy H1 microplate reader

vessel.basis: 25 µL total reaction volume and CFX96 RT-PCR instrument with FRET filter are consistent with a standard 96-well qPCR plate (typical ThermoFluor/DSF protocol, ref. [30]); plate format not stated outright in the text

vessel.notes: described only as 'a 25 mL solution' in a shaking water bath; exact vessel not specified

sampling.context: Two selective-conversion experiments (pure galacturonic acid; pectin hydrolysate)

strategy.notes: fixed time points, no event-triggered/specialised sampling described

sampling.vessel_opened_note: Not explicitly stated; implied yes (aliquots withdrawn manually)

preprocessing.quenching_method: heat inactivation, 95°C for 10 min, per sample
preprocessing.treatment_procedure: HPLC (Ionpak KC-811 column, 85°C, 3 mM H2SO4 eluent, PDA detection 210 nm) and HPAEC-PAD (Carbopac PA-1 column, 30°C, water/0.25 M NaOH/0.65 M NaOAc eluent gradient, pulsed amperometric detection)

sampling.notes: Organic acids below 0.001 wt% (HPLC) and carbohydrates below 0.01% w/w (HPAEC-PAD) treated as below detection limit by the authors.

kinetics.conditions: 25°C, 50 mM KPi, pH 7.0; Michaelis-Menten fit; initial rates in triplicate (Fig. S4)

activity.note: Not reported; enzyme dosing in conversion experiments given only as volumetric activity (U/mL, see biocatalyst.application). Relative-activity substrate scope reported instead (see reaction_components.substrates_screened_table1).

yield_and_conversion.result: Near-complete conversion to galactaric acid within 24 h (curves cross ~5-10 h); no other organic acids above 0.001 wt% detected
Selective, essentially complete oxidation of GalA fraction (0.32 wt% -> trace) to galactaric acid (up to 0.364 wt% at 24 h); glucose, arabinose, galactose (combined 0.11 wt%) unconverted throughout

yield_and_conversion.experiment: Sugar beet pulp hydrolysate (0.36 wt% GalA)
yield_and_conversion.result: Selective and nearly complete conversion of galacturonic acid into galactaric acid (reported qualitatively; data described as 'not shown')

selectivity.chemoselectivity: Demonstrated (not numerically scored): URAOCs3 oxidizes only the uronic-acid component (D-galacturonic acid) of complex sugar mixtures while leaving D-glucose, L-arabinose, D-galactose fully unconverted (Fig. 4A); Table 1 shows <1.1% relative activity on any tested neutral sugar or amino-sugar
selectivity.note: Not applicable/not reported: galacturonic/glucuronic acid oxidation as studied here is not a stereocenter-forming reaction.

thermal_stability.method: ThermoFluor/differential scanning fluorimetry (SYPRO orange dye, FRET filter, CFX96 RT-PCR instrument), temperature ramp 0.5°C/30s. ThermoFAD method could not be used because the flavin is covalently bound.

measurements.condition_varied: pH 5.0-8.0, 50 mM buffer, no added NaCl
measurements.result: Tm 80-84°C across the range; lowest (~80°C) at pH 8; highest ~82-84°C around pH 6-7 (values read from plotted curve, Fig. 3A; exact per-pH numbers not tabulated in text)
No significant effect on Tm despite NaCl reducing activity up to 50% at 500 mM

measurements.condition_varied: D-galacturonic acid 0-1.0 M, 50 mM KPi, pH 7.0
measurements.result: Tm increased by ~5°C at 1.0 M substrate (~82.5°C at 0 M to ~89°C at 1.0 M, read from Fig. 3B)

thermal_stability.schema_note: No dedicated Tm/thermostability field exists in the current StrendaBiocatalysis model; mapped here and to KineticResults.enzyme_stability.

out_of_schema_data.note: The following are reported in the paper but have no corresponding field in the StrendaBiocatalysis schema as currently defined; listed for completeness, not a compliance gap of the paper.
out_of_schema_data.active_site_architecture: Two-domain VAO fold: F-domain (N-term-228 + 454-C-term), S-domain (229-453); bicovalent FAD via His89/Cys151; bound chloride ion near Tyr91-OH (3.2 A) and Arg351-NH2 (3.5 A); active-site residues Tyr91, Tyr165, Arg265, Arg351, Asn383, Lys408, Gln410, Tyr452

substrate_docking.result: Docked galacturonic acid places C6-carboxylate near Arg351 (3.1 A) and C1-OH near Tyr452 (3.0 A), suggesting Tyr452 as catalytic base for hydride transfer to FAD-N5

comparative_structural_analysis.note: Conserved Lys-Arg-Lys (K-R-K) motif present in C. sinensis homologs but not in GOOX (Ala instead of Arg)

out_of_schema_data.bioinformatic_discovery_pipeline: PHI-BLAST of GOOX (Acremonium strictum, UniProt Q6PW77) against predicted C. sinensis proteome, filtered for conserved flavinylation Cys/His and a positively charged residue (Arg/Lys) near the position equivalent to Ala351 in GOOX (based on structural inspection of GOOX:substrate-analog complex, PDB 2AXR)
out_of_schema_data.native_source_isolation: 2 kg oranges -> 470 g peel, homogenized (blender + UltraTurrax 14000 rpm) in 50 mM Tris-HCl/150 mM NaCl/5% glycerol pH 7.5; clarified 3430 x g 1 h; Phenyl-Sepharose HIC to remove pigments; concentrated by 30 kDa-cutoff ultrafiltration; identified as KDO75192.1 (URAOCs1) by in-gel flavin fluorescence + tryptic-peptide MS/MS (29 unique peptides, Fig. S2)

strenda_compliance_report.framing: Assesses how fully the paper's text covers the StrendaBiocatalysis data model, not how well the model fits the paper.
well_covered: Biocatalyst identity (name, origin/production organism, cofactor PTM)
Source and production route for both expression hosts (cloning vectors, purification)
Reaction components: 16-sugar substrate panel with quantified relative activities
Two kinetically characterized substrates with Km, kcat, kcat/Km and fit method
Reaction conditions: temperature and pH, with explicit optimum and full pH-activity/pH-stability scans
Applied yield/conversion/selectivity in pure solution and two independent complex mixtures

gaps.gap: No EC number assigned anywhere in the paper.
No full amino-acid or DNA sequence for URAOCs3 printed in main text or SI; only external accession given.
Purity/grade and supplier not stated for substrates (galacturonic acid, glucuronic acid, screening sugars).
Storage buffer given but no storage temperature, duration, or activity-retention data.
Vessel material, size, geometry, supplier never specified for assays, kinetics, or conversion reactions.
Shaking type and vessel position not given for 110 rpm water-bath incubations; no mixing parameters for microplate assays.
No pH electrode/instrument, calibration standards, or measurement temperature given.
Not stated whether/how vessel was opened for sampling, or headspace gas handling (relevant since O2 is a cosubstrate).
Enzyme dosing reported only volumetrically (U/mL); no U/mg specific activity given.
No cooperativity or formal Ki analysis; salt inhibition shown only qualitatively (Fig. 2B).
All reactions are batch; no flow-rate or feeding-strategy data exist.

optional_additions: Deposit the URAOCs3 amino-acid/DNA sequence directly in the paper or SI, and add a UniProt/GenBank cross-reference table for all four URAOCs1-4 sequences.
Report specific activity (U/mg) alongside volumetric activity (U/mL), using the enzyme concentration already determined by epsilon445.
State vessel type/material/volume for the water-bath conversion experiments.
Fit the salt-inhibition data (Fig. 2B) to an explicit inhibition model (type + Ki).
Note storage temperature/duration and any activity loss observed between purification and use.
strenda_compliance_report.integrity_note: Every gap above is a genuine absence in the published text/SI, not a modeling artifact. This extraction did not fill any gap with an assumed number; the only non-stated additions (O2 as cosubstrate, general EC-classification context, unverified glucaric-acid product) are each marked stated_in_paper: false with their own basis, distinct from the paper's own data.
